- Fittix is built on the [AddressBook-Level3 project](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3); the original architecture, setup guide, and some diagrams were adapted for this project.
- The desktop interface uses [JavaFX](https://openjfx.io/), and the documentation site uses [Jekyll](https://jekyllrb.com/) with the [Minima theme](https://github.com/jekyll/minima).

- The interface bundles the [Manrope](https://github.com/sharanda/manrope) and [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/) fonts under the SIL Open Font License; their licence files are in `src/main/resources/fonts/`.
- Architecture and design diagrams were created with [PlantUML](https://plantuml.com/).
Refer to the guide [_Setting up and getting started_](SettingUp.md).

The **_Architecture Diagram_** given above explains the high-level design of the App.
The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T14-1/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T14-1/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
- At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
- At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
- [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
- [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**

Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),

- provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

The workspace has three columns inside one scroll pane: `PersonListPanel` displays clients and manages selection, `ClientDetailPanel` shows the selected client's profile and workout plan, and `ClientContextPanel` shows their diet, restrictions, appointments, workout history, body progress, and payments. `ClientContextPanel` owns a `BodyProgressPanel` for baseline measurements, progress history, and the latest comparison. These visible controllers, together with `MainWindow`, `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `HelpWindow`, `PersonCard`, and `StatusBarFooter`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart<T>` class, which loads their FXML and exposes their root node.

`MainWindow` creates and retains the main panels, command box, result display, and help window. It also creates a `StatusBarFooter` locally and supplies the save path and the list panel's observable client count. The footer binds its count label to that property. The list panel builds one `PersonCard` per displayed client into a `VBox`, rebuilding the cards when the filtered list changes, so the workspace has a single scrollbar; it does not retain a separate card controller for every client. Selecting a client moves the `selected` style class between the existing cards. The panel reports selection changes, and explicit reveal requests, to `MainWindow`, which scrolls the workspace only as far as needed to show the selected card. The command box and result display sit in a terminal panel below the workspace; `MainWindow` adds it to the workspace `SplitPane` when it opens, removes it when it closes, and remembers its height in `GuiSettings`.

`CommandBox` receives a `CommandExecutor` callback supplied as `MainWindow`'s `this::executeCommand` method reference. `MainWindow` calls `Logic.execute`, appends results or errors to `ResultDisplay`, and updates selection and filter indicators. `CommandCatalog` supplies command hints and help details. `ResultDisplay` retains up to 50 immutable `CommandFeedback` entries for its scrolling history. `MainWindow` does not implement the callback interface itself.

`MainWindow` listens to the list panel's selection and the observable client data supplied by `Logic`, then refreshes both selected-client panels. A `CommandResult` may also contain a `BodyProgressViewRequest`; after a successful body-progress command, `MainWindow` selects the resolved client, passes the request to `ClientContextPanel`, and scrolls the shared workspace to the requested tracker section. UI controllers display `Person` data from the Model component.

The `UI` component uses JavaFX. Layouts are defined in `.fxml` resources under `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T14-1/tp/blob/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) defines the layout loaded by [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T14-1/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java). The diagram omits individual JavaFX controls, private rendering helpers, and the detailed Model classes to keep the component relationships readable.

For an ordinary command such as `delete 1`, the current execution boundary is:
1. `AddressBookParser` delegates to the matching parser and returns a validated `Command`. A parsing failure leaves the model unchanged.

1. `LogicManager` snapshots the complete address book and the current client predicate, then executes the command against the model. The command returns a `CommandResult` or throws a `CommandException`.

1. If the address book equals its snapshot, `LogicManager` returns the result without writing a file or changing undo/redo history. Changes to the displayed search filter alone do not require saving client data.

1. Otherwise, `LogicManager` saves the changed address book. A successful save pushes the snapshot onto the bounded undo stack and clears redo. A failed save restores both the data and predicate and throws the appropriate save error, leaving history intact.

1. The UI receives a successful result only after this boundary completes. The architecture sequence above shows the effective-change path for workout logging; the body-progress and undo/redo sections illustrate successful saves and rollback in more detail.
`UndoCommand` and `RedoCommand` take the separate snapshot-restoration paths described in the [undo/redo implementation](#undo-redo-implementation).

`StorageManager` implements `Storage` and delegates JSON file access to one `JsonAddressBookStorage` and one `JsonUserPrefsStorage`. The overview shows these services and the top-level JSON representation. Model classes and common JSON/file utilities are omitted to keep the view focused on the storage component.

`JsonSerializableAddressBook` contains the saved clients and shared membership-plan catalog. Each `JsonAdaptedPerson` retains adapters for its tags, exercises, optional diet plan, scheduled sessions, recorded workouts, payment records, optional membership assignment and optional body tracker. Its payment-history list retains zero or more `JsonAdaptedPaymentRecord` instances, each storing an amount, date and optional remarks. The detail diagram expands these client adapters; its multiplicities describe supported, validated data. In particular, a recorded workout contains 1 to 30 exercise entries.
<div class="diagram-scroll" role="region" tabindex="0" aria-label="Client JSON adapters and nested conversion dependencies">

A membership assignment stores a plan key rather than a reference to `JsonAdaptedMembershipPlan`; loading validates that key against the catalog. `JsonAdaptedBodyProgress` retains a raw `JsonNode` and uses the baseline/entry adapters temporarily during conversion, so those helper relationships are dependencies rather than retained associations. Goal, health information and dietary restrictions are stored as strings or lists of strings and therefore have no separate adapter classes in these diagrams.

The storage component reads JSON back into the corresponding model objects and saves model data in JSON form. It therefore depends on model classes even though those dependencies are outside the scope of the two diagrams.

`MainApp#initModelManager` uses sample data only when the client file is absent. A `DataLoadingException` for an existing file aborts initialization before `LogicManager` is created. This prevents a subsequent command from overwriting unreadable data with an empty address book. The original file remains available for recovery after correcting the local date/time zone or restoring a backup. New future-dated workout input and invalid saved workout dates are still rejected.
Classes used by multiple components are in the `seedu.address.commons` package.
This section describes some noteworthy details on how certain features are implemented.

Each `Person` stores an immutable list of `TrainingSession` appointments. A session contains a `LocalDateTime`, a nonblank location, and a `Kind` of `TRAINING` or `MEETING`. `Person#withTrainingSession` returns a replacement person with the new appointment appended; the commands do not mutate the existing person. `JsonAdaptedTrainingSession` persists the appointment type alongside its date, time, and location. For compatibility with older saved data, a missing type is read as `TRAINING`.

`ScheduleCommandParser` and `MeetingCommandParser` use `AppointmentParser` to validate the displayed-list index, real calendar date, 24-hour time, nonblank location, and a start time later than the current local time. Their commands delegate to `AppointmentScheduler#add`. It searches the **entire** address book, including clients hidden by a filter, for an appointment with the same start time. If one exists, it reports the conflicting client and makes no change. Otherwise, it replaces the selected client with one containing the new appointment. Training sessions and meetings use the same conflict check. Because no duration is stored, appointments at different start times can still overlap in practice.

`ViewScheduleCommand` sorts one displayed client's appointments by start time; meetings are marked in the result. `DayScheduleCommand` instead scans all clients for the requested date, then orders appointments by start time and client name. Both commands are read-only. `InactiveCommand` also scans the full roster: for `inactive DAYS`, it calculates `today - (DAYS - 1)` and lists clients with no **completed workout log** on or after that date. A scheduled session or meeting does not count as a workout. The inactive list is ordered by client name and includes the latest recorded workout date, if any. `ClientContextPanel` labels meeting rows separately from training sessions, and `CommandCatalog` supplies usage hints for all five scheduling and monitoring commands.
For repeatable command checks, see [Scheduling and client monitoring acceptance checks](#manual-scheduling-and-monitoring).

The workout plan feature lets a trainer keep a per-client list of prescribed exercises, optionally scheduled by weekday. Each `Person` owns one immutable `WorkoutPlan` (possibly empty); each `Exercise` is immutable and validated at construction. Plans are always kept sorted Monday-to-Sunday, with unscheduled exercises last.
- name is valid when `!test.trim().isEmpty()`; failure message is `Exercise name should not be blank`.
- sets/reps are valid when `> 0`; failure messages are `Sets should be a positive integer greater than 0` and `Reps should be a positive integer greater than 0`.
- weight is valid when `Double.isFinite(test) && test >= 0`; failure message is `Weight should be a finite non-negative number in kg`.
- Combined message is `Exercise name should not be blank, sets and reps should be positive integers greater than 0, and weight should be a finite non-negative number in kg`.

- Command parsers supply the canonical full weekday name (`Monday`…`Sunday`) or `""` for unscheduled exercises. The constructor trims the input and normalizes legacy values: anything equal (ignoring case) to `Day not specified` becomes `""`. `Exercise#withDay(day)` returns a copy assigned to a new day; `Exercise#getDay` returns the stored value.

- Identity is name-based case-insensitive (`Exercise#isSameExercise`); full equality also compares sets/reps/weight/day. Duplicate checking in `WorkoutPlan#hasExercise` additionally compares the day, resolving weekday prefixes and ignoring letter case. Unassigned exercises share one group; matching names on different days are allowed. `SetExerciseDayCommand` checks for a duplicate on the destination day after excluding the selected exercise.
- `model.person.Weekday` is the canonical weekday enum (`MONDAY`…`SUNDAY` with display names `Monday`…`Sunday`).

- `Weekday#fromPrefix` resolves a case-insensitive full name or prefix: minimum length is 1 except `Tuesday`/`Thursday`/`Sunday`, which need at least 2 characters. Hence a lone `s` means Saturday (Sunday needs `su`), and a lone `t` is invalid (`tu` = Tuesday, `th` = Thursday).
- `Weekday#sortOrder(day)` returns the weekday rank (Monday 0 … Sunday 6); missing or unrecognized days sort after Sunday.

- `model.person.WorkoutPlan` wraps `List<Exercise>` with defensive copies and an unmodifiable view (`#getExercises`). Every constructor and mutator re-sorts by `Weekday.sortOrder` (a stable sort, so exercises in the same day group keep their relative order). Key APIs: `#hasExercise` (duplicate check), `#addExercise` (returns new plan), `#removeExercise`, `#setExerciseDay(index, day)` (replaces the exercise at the zero-based index via `Exercise#withDay` and re-sorts), `#isEmpty`, `#size`. `Person` stores the plan and exposes it via `#getWorkoutPlan`; `PersonBuilder#withWorkoutPlan` is used in tests.

- `WorkoutPlan#isWithinDailyLimit` checks a weekday against `MAX_EXERCISES_PER_DAY` (7), resolving weekday prefixes and letter case through `Weekday#fromPrefix`. Unassigned exercises have no daily limit. `AddExerciseCommand` and `SetExerciseDayCommand` check the destination day in the proposed immutable plan before updating the model. A violation produces `Messages.MESSAGE_DAILY_EXERCISE_LIMIT` and leaves the model unchanged. Checking the proposed plan allows reassignment to the same day at capacity and moving exercises away from a full day. Existing saved plans are still loaded without truncation.

- `MESSAGE_USAGE = addex: Adds an exercise to the workout plan of the person identified by the index number used in the last person listing. Parameters: INDEX (must be a positive integer) n/EXERCISE_NAME [s/SETS] [r/REPS] [w/WEIGHT_KG] [d/DAY] Example: addex 1 n/Bench Press s/3 r/10 w/60 d/M`.
- Success message `MESSAGE_ADD_EXERCISE_SUCCESS = Added exercise to Person: %1$s` (formatted with `Messages.format(editedPerson)`).
- Duplicate message `MESSAGE_DUPLICATE_EXERCISE = This exercise already exists on this day in the workout plan.`

- `execute` checks `Messages.MESSAGE_INVALID_PERSON_DISPLAYED_INDEX` (`The person index provided is invalid.`) for an out-of-range person index, rejects duplicates, then builds a new `Person` with `WorkoutPlan#addExercise` and calls `model#setPerson` + `model#updateFilteredPersonList(PREDICATE_SHOW_ALL_PERSONS)`.

- `MESSAGE_USAGE = delex: Removes the exercise at the specified exercise index from the workout plan of the person identified by the index number used in the last person listing. Parameters: PERSON_INDEX EXERCISE_INDEX (both must be positive integers) Example: delex 1 2`.
- Success message `MESSAGE_DELETE_EXERCISE_SUCCESS = Removed exercise from Person: %1$s`.
- Invalid exercise message `MESSAGE_INVALID_EXERCISE_DISPLAYED_INDEX = The exercise index provided is invalid.` shown when `exerciseIndex` is out of range, including when the plan is empty.

- `execute` checks the person index first (`MESSAGE_INVALID_PERSON_DISPLAYED_INDEX`), then the exercise index, removes that entry from a copy of the list, wraps it in a new `WorkoutPlan`, and saves via `model#setPerson`. The exercise index is the current display number (see feedback formatting below), not the raw insertion order.
- `MESSAGE_USAGE = dayex: Assigns a day tag to an exercise in a person's workout plan. Parameters: PERSON_INDEX EXERCISE_INDEX DAY Example: dayex 1 2 Tuesday`.
- Success message `MESSAGE_SUCCESS = Assigned day to exercise: %1$s` (formatted with `Messages.format(editedPerson)`).
- Invalid exercise message `MESSAGE_INVALID_EXERCISE_INDEX = The exercise index provided is invalid.` shown when `exerciseIndex` is out of range, including when the plan is empty.

- `execute` checks the person index first (`MESSAGE_INVALID_PERSON_DISPLAYED_INDEX`), then the exercise index, applies `WorkoutPlan#setExerciseDay` (which re-sorts Monday-to-Sunday and renumbers), and saves via `model#setPerson` + `model#updateFilteredPersonList(PREDICATE_SHOW_ALL_PERSONS)`.

- `MESSAGE_USAGE = clearplan: Clears all exercises from the workout plan of the person identified by the index number used in the last person listing. Parameters: INDEX (must be a positive integer) Example: clearplan 1`.

- Success `MESSAGE_CLEAR_PLAN_SUCCESS = Cleared workout plan for Person: %1$s`; already-empty `MESSAGE_PLAN_ALREADY_EMPTY = Workout plan is already empty for Person: %1$s` (no model change in the latter case).

- Parsers: `AddExerciseCommandParser` rejects unknown alphabetic parameter prefixes before tokenizing with `n/ s/ r/ w/ d/`; only `n/` is required, while omitted sets, reps, and weight default to `1`, `1`, and `0`. An omitted `d/` stores `""` (rendered under the `Day not specified` heading); a provided `d/` value is resolved via `DayParserUtil#parseDay` to the canonical weekday name. It rejects duplicates via `verifyNoDuplicatePrefixesFor` and delegates provided values to the matching `ParserUtil` validation methods (`parseExerciseName/Sets/Reps/Weight`); empty values such as `s/` or `d/` therefore fail validation. Any `ParseException` is wrapped as `Invalid command format!` + `MESSAGE_USAGE`. `DeleteExerciseCommandParser` expects exactly two indices (`PERSON_INDEX EXERCISE_INDEX`); `ClearPlanCommandParser` expects exactly one index; both wrap failures the same way. `SetExerciseDayCommandParser` splits the trimmed args on whitespace and requires exactly three parts (`PERSON_INDEX EXERCISE_INDEX DAY`), parsing the indices with `ParserUtil#parseIndex` and the day with `DayParserUtil#parseDay`, wrapping failures as `Invalid command format!` + `SetExerciseDayCommand.MESSAGE_USAGE`. `DayParserUtil#parseDay` delegates to `Weekday#fromPrefix` and returns the canonical display name, throwing `ParseException("Invalid day")` for anything else (e.g. `t`, `funday`, or the `Day not specified` heading). `AddressBookParser` routes `addex`/`delex`/`dayex`/`clearplan` to these parsers; unknown words return `Unknown command.`

- Feedback formatting: `Messages#format(Person)` appends `; Workout Plan: ` + `formatWorkoutPlan(plan)`, where an empty plan renders as `Empty` and a non-empty plan renders grouped by day in Monday-to-Sunday order with **Day not specified** last, e.g. `(4):` followed by `**Monday**`, `1. Squat 4x8 @80kg`, blank line, `**Wednesday**`, `2. Bench Press 3x10 @60kg`, and so on via `formatExercise` (`%s %dx%d @%skg`, e.g. `Bench Press 3x10 @60kg`, trimming `.0` weights). `Messages#getExercisesInDisplayOrder` re-sorts a copy of the plan the same way and assigns continuous 1-based numbers across all groups; `Messages#getExerciseDayHeading` maps `""` to `Day not specified` and any stored day through `Weekday#fromPrefix` to its display name. These numbers are exactly the `EXERCISE_INDEX` values accepted by `delex` and `dayex`, and appear after `%1$s` in all four success messages.

- `storage.JsonAdaptedExercise` is the Jackson-friendly form with fields `name`, `sets`, `reps`, `weightKg`, `day`. `toModelType` throws `IllegalValueException` with `Exercise's %s field is missing!` for null `name`/`sets`/`reps`/`weightKg`, or the matching `Exercise.MESSAGE_CONSTRAINTS_*` message for invalid values, and rejects non-finite/negative weights. A missing, `null`, or blank `day`, and legacy `Day not specified` values (ignoring case), load as unscheduled. Other saved values are resolved with `Weekday#fromPrefix` and stored as canonical full names; an unrecognized value fails loading with `Invalid exercise day: VALUE` instead of being silently accepted.

- `storage.JsonAdaptedPerson` persists the plan as JSON array `exercises`. The `@JsonCreator` constructor treats a missing/`null` `exercises` field as empty (backward compatible with old files). `toModelType` rejects `null` entries with `Workout plan must not contain null exercises`, converts each entry via `JsonAdaptedExercise#toModelType`, and builds `new WorkoutPlan(personExercises)` (which re-sorts by weekday). Any invalid exercise therefore fails the whole person load, which `JsonSerializableAddressBook` propagates as `IllegalValueException`; startup then stops before creating the command-processing logic, preserving the original file instead of opening an empty roster that could overwrite it.

- Save path: `JsonAdaptedPerson(Person source)` copies `source.getWorkoutPlan().getExercises()` into adapted exercises (including each exercise's canonical `day`), so every `addex`/`delex`/`dayex`/`clearplan` is persisted on the next `StorageManager` save (automatic after each mutating command).

`ClientDetailPanel#showWorkoutPlan` renders the selected client's plan in `workoutRows`, using `Messages#getExercisesInDisplayOrder` for the continuous 1-based numbers shared with command feedback. `PersonCard` renders the client-list summary; it does not render the workout plan.

- The card heading is `Workout plan`. A nonempty plan also shows the exercise count and number of assigned training days in `planSummary`. An empty plan leaves the summary blank and hides `workoutRows`, so only the heading remains visible.

- `createDayRow` renders all seven weekdays in Monday-to-Sunday order, with uppercase day codes (`MON` through `SUN`) and full weekday subtitles. Days without exercises show `Rest`. Unscheduled exercises appear in a final `Day not specified` row created by `createUnspecifiedRow`.

- `createExerciseTile` shows the current exercise number in a separate numeric badge (`1`, `2`, …), a wrapping name, sets × reps, and weight. Zero weight displays as `BW`; other weights display in kg. Each day lays out up to three tiles per row. The current weekday is highlighted.

- `delex` and `dayex` use the current displayed exercise numbers. Adding, moving or deleting exercises can re-sort and renumber the plan, so trainers must check the updated numbers before the next indexed command.

- `MainWindow` refreshes the selected-client panel after model/list changes. The card grows vertically within the shared workspace scroll pane; it has no internal scrollbar or fixed 350-pixel label width.

Diet goals consist of one current nutrition target and optional coaching notes per client. The implementation retains the existing `DietPlan` model, `dietPlan` JSON field, and command-message wording; the feature rename does not change the command syntax or saved-data format.

Each `Person` owns an optional immutable `DietPlan`, consisting of one required target and optional notes. The model trims outer whitespace, counts Unicode code points, rejects nonprintable characters, and requires at least one letter or digit in the target. It preserves internal text and case. `JsonAdaptedPerson` and `JsonAdaptedDietPlan` serialize the diet goals in the client's JSON record, so deleting the client also removes their diet goals. A client has at most one current target record and no history of diet goals.

For `diet INDEX t/TARGET [n/NOTES]`, `AddressBookParser` passes the raw arguments to `DietCommandParser`. This preserves invalid line breaks for validation. At the beginning of an argument or after horizontal whitespace, the parser reserves single-letter prefixes and markers formed by repeating or mixing `t` and `n` in either case. Only exact lowercase `t/` and `n/` are accepted; mistyped markers such as `nn/`, `tt/`, `nt/`, and `tn/` are rejected before command execution, including inside notes. Other slash-separated words such as `kcal/day` remain ordinary text. It validates the displayed-list index, one required target, at most one optional notes value, and rejects unknown or repeated prefixes. `DietCommand` looks up the `Person` in the filtered list, compares the candidate with the current diet goals after trimming and ignoring case, then uses `Model#setPerson` to replace the client record while retaining the other fields and current list filter. An omitted `n/` saves diet goals without notes, even when the previous record had notes.

`LogicManager` snapshots the address book before executing a diet command. `JsonAddressBookStorage` writes a complete JSON document to a temporary file in the data file's directory, then atomically moves it over the old file. If writing or replacing the file fails, `LogicManager` restores the snapshot and returns `The diet plan could not be saved. The previous plan remains unchanged.` The storage layer does not fall back to a non-atomic replacement when the filesystem does not support atomic moves. Validation and duplicate failures occur before any model change.

After a successful save, the shared undo history retains the previous complete address book and clears the redo history. Rejected diet commands and failed saves create no undo step. A replacement clears omitted notes in the current record, while session-level undo can still restore the previous target and notes. There is no separate diet-history store.

`ClientContextPanel` shows the selected client's diet goals in the right-hand **DIET** section. It shows the current target and notes and hides notes when absent. For a client without diet goals, the section keeps its heading and hides the target and notes. Long accepted values wrap, and the workspace scrolls as a whole. The UI does not evaluate the diet goals' nutritional or medical suitability.

`DietCommandParserTest`, `DietCommandTest`, and `DietIntegrationTest` cover parsing limits, duplicate and replacement behavior, filtered indexes, save and restart, and injected commit failure. `WorkoutSessionDisplayTest#dietPlan_showsTargetAndOptionalNotes` checks the `ClientContextPanel` target text and optional-note visibility. `WorkoutSessionDisplayTest#switchingToClientWithoutRecords_clearsPriorRows` checks that switching to a client without records hides the previous client's diet, appointment and history content. The manual scenarios below cover the main user flows.

Each `Person` owns an immutable `DietaryRestrictions` list, which is empty when no restrictions are recorded. `restriction INDEX r/RESTRICTION [r/RESTRICTION]...` replaces the complete list; one blank sole `r/` clears it. The value object validates 1 to 10 ordered entries, each containing 1 to 100 printable Unicode characters and at least one letter or digit. It rejects duplicates after trimming and case-insensitive comparison while preserving the first supplied display text and ordering.

`DietaryRestrictionsCommandParser` parses a displayed-list index and repeated `r/` values. `DietaryRestrictionsCommand` rejects an unchanged list and replaces the client with `Person#withDietaryRestrictions`, preserving unrelated data. `JsonAdaptedPerson` stores the list as `dietaryRestrictions`; an absent field loads as an empty list for backwards compatibility. `find dr/KEYWORDS` uses `DietaryRestrictionsContainsKeywordsPredicate` and retains the existing OR semantics. The selected-client detail pane only displays the list when nonempty. Restriction text is informational and does not determine allergy or meal safety.

Each `Person` has an optional immutable `HealthProfile` with one current trainer-visible note. `health INDEX h/NOTE` replaces the note and `health INDEX h/` clears it. `HealthProfile` trims outer whitespace, accepts 1 to 500 printable Unicode characters with at least one letter or digit, and rejects line breaks and control characters. The profile is serialized as the optional `healthProfile` field in `JsonAdaptedPerson`; older data without that field loads without a profile.

`HealthCommandParser` requires exactly one `h/` prefix and a displayed-list index. `HealthCommand` rejects a no-op update, replaces the client through `Person#withHealthProfile`, and preserves all unrelated client information. `find h/KEYWORDS` uses `HealthProfileContainsKeywordsPredicate` with the existing case-insensitive OR search behavior. The selected-client details panel displays the profile only when present. Health considerations are informational only; the application does not diagnose conditions or evaluate medical suitability.

`find` has two forms: `find KEYWORD...`, a name search, and `find [n/NAME] [p/PHONE] [e/EMAIL] [g/GOAL] [dr/RESTRICTION] [h/HEALTH]`. Use case UC03 describes only the name form; the user-facing behaviour of all criteria is in the User Guide.

`FindCommandParser` tokenizes the input with the six supported prefixes. With no prefix, the whole trimmed input becomes a name search. With at least one prefix, it rejects a non-empty preamble (a bare keyword cannot be mixed with prefixes), a prefix used more than once, an empty value, and a `p/` value without a digit. It creates one predicate per supplied prefix and wraps them all in a `ClientMatchesAnyPredicate`, which uses `anyMatch`, so a client is shown when it satisfies any one criterion (OR).
| `n/` | `NameContainsKeywordsPredicate` | any whitespace-separated keyword is a case-insensitive substring of the name |
| `p/` | `PhoneMatchesPredicate` | one query; spaces and hyphens are removed from the query and the stored phone, then the phone must contain the query |
| `e/` | `EmailContainsKeywordsPredicate` | any keyword is a case-insensitive substring of the email |
| `g/` | `GoalContainsKeywordsPredicate` | any keyword is a case-insensitive substring of the goal; clients without a goal never match |
| `dr/` | `DietaryRestrictionsContainsKeywordsPredicate` | any keyword is a case-insensitive substring of any current restriction |
| `h/` | `HealthProfileContainsKeywordsPredicate` | any keyword is a case-insensitive substring of the health note; clients without one never match |

Case-insensitive matching lowercases both sides with `Locale.ROOT`, except the name predicate, which uses `StringUtil#containsIgnoreCase`. The health predicate also folds the Greek final sigma (`ς`) to the ordinary sigma (`σ`) after lowercasing, so sigma variants match each other. `FindCommand` passes the combined predicate to `Model#updateFilteredPersonList` and reports `Found N client(s).` or the zero-result message. It does not modify stored data.

OR was chosen so that each additional criterion widens the result and so that each feature can contribute its own predicate without changing the others. To add a criterion, define a prefix in `CliSyntax`, add it to `FindCommandParser#SUPPORTED_PREFIXES`, write a `Predicate<Person>` in `model.person`, and add a branch to `FindCommandParser#createFindCommand`. Automated coverage is in `FindCommandParserTest`, `FindCommandTest`, `ClientMatchesAnyPredicateTest` and one test class per predicate.
Each `Person` owns an immutable list of `WorkoutSession` objects. Each session contains a required `LocalDate`, an optional `LocalTime`, and an ordered list of 1 to 30 `WorkoutLogEntry` objects.

`WorkoutSession` rejects future dates, times containing seconds or nanoseconds, empty exercise lists, and lists exceeding the entry limit. Each `WorkoutLogEntry` validates its exercise name, weight, sets, and repetitions. Weight uses `BigDecimal` and is displayed with `toPlainString()`.

For `log INDEX d/DATE [t/TIME] ex/EXERCISE|WEIGHT|SETS|REPS ...`, `AddressBookParser` delegates to `LogCommandParser`. The parser checks required arguments, repeated date or time prefixes, date and time formats, and the four values in every exercise entry. It constructs the complete validated session before returning a `LogCommand`.

`LogCommand` resolves the index against the filtered client list. It rejects a session if that client already has the same date and optional time, using `WorkoutSession#hasSameDateTime`. Exercise contents do not affect this duplicate check. An unspecified time is distinct from every specified time. Duplicate feedback identifies the client and date, includes the time when specified, and otherwise explains that the collision has unspecified time and suggests adding `t/TIME`.

On success, the command appends the session to a copy of the existing session list and replaces the client through `Model#setPerson`, preserving their other fields and the current filter. Sessions remain in recording order rather than chronological order. Success feedback includes the client, an English `d MMM uuuu` date, optional `HH:mm` time, and the number of exercise entries, using `1 exercise` or `N exercises`. Repeated entries are counted separately.

`JsonAdaptedWorkoutLogEntry`, `JsonAdaptedWorkoutSession`, and `JsonAdaptedPerson` handle persistence. Dates use `yyyy-MM-dd`, specified times use `HH:mm`, and exercise order is preserved. Older person records without a workout-session field load with an empty session list. Invalid entries and duplicate session keys are rejected during conversion to model objects.

`LogicManager` saves the updated address book through the storage component. If saving throws an `IOException`, it restores the address-book snapshot taken before command execution and reports the save error.

It sorts a copy by date descending, then places unspecified times before specified times on the same date, with specified times descending. Unspecified times are distinct from midnight and display as `Time not specified`. The stored recording order and exercise order are unchanged. For a client without sessions, the section shows `No workout sessions recorded for NAME.` instead of session rows. - `AddressBook` owns an insertion-ordered collection of uniquely named `MembershipPlan` definitions. A plan has a normalized display name, a positive `BigDecimal` price stored at two decimal places, and 1 to 1000 starting sessions. Names are compared without regard to case after trimming and collapsing internal whitespace.

- Each `Person` has at most one optional `MembershipAssignment`. It keeps a reference to the shared plan, a copy of its display name, an independent remaining balance from 0 to 1000, and an optional expiry date. Assigning a plan copies its starting sessions; subsequent adjustments change only that client's balance. A referenced plan cannot be deleted.

- JSON stores `membershipPlans` at the address-book root and `membershipAssignment` on each person. Missing fields in older files mean an empty catalog or an unassigned client. Loading rejects duplicate plan keys, null plan or person entries, malformed values, assignments referring to missing plans, and assignments whose copied plan name disagrees with the plan their key points to. Expired assignments remain loadable; expiry is checked against the local date only when `amem` runs.

- Address-book snapshots and person replacement copy membership data. On an `IOException` during save, `LogicManager` restores the complete pre-command state and reports that the membership change could not be saved.

`AddressBookParser` routes `addmem n/NAME p/PRICE s/NUMBER_OF_SESSIONS`, `delmem n/NAME`, `amem MEMBERSHIP_NAME PERSON_INDEX [e/YYYY-MM-DD]`, `rmem PERSON_INDEX`, `imem PERSON_INDEX NUMBER_TO_INCREMENT`, `dmem PERSON_INDEX NUMBER_TO_DECREMENT`, `clearmem`, and both `view mem` and `view membership`. Command words and the `view` argument are case-sensitive; prefix letters and plan name matching are case-insensitive. Client indexes refer to the currently displayed client list. For `amem`, the final non-prefixed token before an optional `e/` is the client index, allowing spaces in the plan name.

`ClearmemCommand` (`COMMAND_WORD = clearmem`, `MESSAGE_SUCCESS = Cleared all membership plans.`) takes no parameters and deletes every plan in the catalog while leaving all other data, including client records, workout plans, schedules, diet goals, and workout logs, unchanged. Before deleting, it checks whether any plan is referenced by a client assignment. If so, it deletes nothing and returns `MESSAGE_PLANS_IN_USE = Membership plans are in use and cannot be cleared. Remove all client assignments with rmem first.`, consistent with `delmem`'s rule that a referenced plan cannot be deleted. The client `clear` command (`ClearCommand`) is the counterpart for client records: it removes all persons only and must not delete any membership plans, so it bypasses the in-use check. Either command persists its result through the automatic save after the command runs.

Parsers require each mandatory prefix exactly once, reject repeated or unknown prefixes and extra text, and validate prices, session counts, and dates before changing the model. `amem` requires a future expiry date when one is supplied. `imem` and `dmem` accept amounts from 1 to 1000 and keep the resulting balance within 0 to 1000. A client with an assignment must use `rmem` before receiving another plan. Both view aliases show the same plan order and `No membership plans available.` when the catalog is empty.

The client card shows a single membership tag reading `Plan_name Member: N sessions left`, with `[expires YYYY-MM-DD]` appended when an expiry exists and the plan name's first letter upper-cased. The tag joins the client's other tags in the card's tag area, directly under the name, and wraps within the card, so a long plan name does not push the balance or expiry outside it. Implemented for v1.4. The [feature contract](featureSpecs.md#feature-14-payment-records) defines user-visible behavior. `pay` appends one immutable payment to a client's history; it does not change a membership assignment, plan price, or session balance.

- `model.person.PaymentRecord` is an immutable payment containing a `BigDecimal amount` (normalized to two decimal places), a `LocalDate date`, and an optional `remarks`. It exposes `fromText` and the `parse*`/`isValid*` helpers for raw input and validation, reused by parsing and storage.

- `amount` is positive with no precision beyond two decimals; `AMOUNT_SCALE` is 2. It is stored and displayed via `BigDecimal.toPlainString()`, so there is no floating-point rounding and `75`, `75.5`, and `75.50` are equivalent. `AMOUNT_PATTERN` (`\d+(\.\d{1,2})?`) rejects signs, currency symbols, thousands separators, and over-precise or malformed text.
- `date` must match `uuuu-MM-dd` with a `ResolverStyle.STRICT` formatter and year 0001–9999. Past, current, and future dates are all accepted.

- `remarks` is optional; when present it trims outer horizontal whitespace, counts Unicode code points (1–300, `MAX_REMARKS_LENGTH`), and rejects ISO control, format, line/paragraph separator, surrogate, private-use, and unassigned code points. Internal spacing and case are preserved.

- `Person` owns an insertion-ordered `List<PaymentRecord>` (`paymentRecords`). `withAddedPayment` copies the list and appends the new record. Every other client-update command (`diet`, `edit`, `editlog`, `remark`, and the workout-plan, workout-logging, membership, and body-progress commands) constructs a new `Person` passing `person.getPaymentRecords()` through, so payments are preserved across unrelated edits. Deleting a client removes their payments with the client.

- JSON stores `paymentRecords` on each person. `JsonAdaptedPerson` initializes the field to an empty list, so a missing/null `paymentRecords` field in older files loads an empty payment history. `toModelType` rejects null entries (`Payment records must not contain null entries.`) and converts each entry via `JsonAdaptedPaymentRecord#toModelType`, preserving entry order and never deduplicating, so repeated payments stay distinct.

- `storage.JsonAdaptedPaymentRecord` is the Jackson form with required `amount` and `date` strings and a `@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)` `remarks` string. `toModelType` throws `IllegalValueException` with `Payment record's %s field is missing!` for a null `amount`/`date`, and maps invalid stored values to the `PaymentRecord` constraint messages.

- `MESSAGE_USAGE = pay: Records a payment for the client identified by the index number used in the displayed client list.\nParameters: INDEX (must be a positive integer) a/AMOUNT d/YYYY-MM-DD [r/REMARKS]\nExample: pay 1 a/150 d/2026-10-20`.
- Success `MESSAGE_SUCCESS = Recorded payment for %1$s: %2$s on %3$s.`, formatted with `updated.getName()`, `paymentRecord.getFormattedAmount()`, and `paymentRecord.getDate()`.
- `MESSAGE_SAVE_FAILURE = Payment could not be saved. No payment was recorded.`

- `execute` resolves the index against `getFilteredPersonList()`, rejects an out-of-range index with `Messages.MESSAGE_INVALID_PERSON_DISPLAYED_INDEX`, builds `target.withAddedPayment(paymentRecord)`, and updates the in-memory model via `model#setPerson` (replacing only that person while preserving the client's other fields and the current filter). `LogicManager` then persists the changed address book through Storage (rolling the payment back if the write fails, as described at the end of this item).

- `logic.parser.PayCommandParser` reads the displayed index, then the prefixed `a/` (`CliSyntax.PREFIX_ADDRESS`), `d/` (`CliSyntax.PREFIX_DATE`), and optional `r/` (`CliSyntax.PREFIX_REMARK`) values. The command word and prefixes are matched case-sensitively. `AddressBookParser` routes `pay` with a `DOTALL` pattern (AddressBookParser.java:62) and the parser keeps raw arguments until validation so an embedded line break survives to be rejected (`containsLineBreak`); any line break produces `Invalid command format!` + `MESSAGE_USAGE`. It rejects a blank index or argument area, a repeated/unknown/empty prefix, an unknown `word/`-style token inside a value (e.g. `x/`), and extra unprefixed text. `a/` and `d/` are required and must be single tokens (internal whitespace is rejected), while a single empty `r/` is rejected. Validated values are built into a `PaymentRecord` via `PaymentRecord.fromText` before a `PayCommand` is returned.

- `LogicManager` maps an `IOException` from a `PayCommand` to `PayCommand.MESSAGE_SAVE_FAILURE`, so a failed write restores the previous payment data in memory and on disk, exactly like `diet`, membership, and body mutations.
- `ui.CommandCatalog` registers `PayCommand` for usage hints and the help window.

The remarks, date and amount wrap instead of being truncated. Selection changes rebuild the rows, so switching clients never leaves a stale payment row.

1.  Should run on supported Windows, macOS and Linux systems with a compatible Java `25` installation, without a separate JavaFX installation.
2.  Should be delivered as a single JAR file of at most 100MB that runs without an installer.
3.  Should work fully offline, with no dependency on a remote server or network connection.
4.  Should be able to hold up to 1000 clients without noticeable sluggishness in performance for typical usage.
5.  Every command should return a visible response within 2 seconds when the data file holds 1000 clients.

6.  A user with above average typing speed for regular English text (i.e. not code, not system admin commands) should be able to accomplish most of the tasks faster using commands than using the mouse.
7.  Logging a completed workout session should require a single command line, so that a user with above average typing speed can complete it in under 15 seconds between sets.
8.  Data should be saved to disk after every command that modifies it, so an unexpected shutdown loses at most the command in progress.
9.  Data should be stored locally in a human editable text file, with no database management system.

10. If the client data file is missing, the app should load the bundled sample clients. If an existing file cannot be read or validated, startup should stop with an explanatory error and preserve that file, rather than open an empty replacement roster.
11. Error messages should state what was rejected and the expected format, so the user can correct the command without consulting the user guide.

12. The supported minimum application window is 1280x800 logical pixels. Display scaling requires proportionally more physical screen space; layout and text readability should be checked on each supported OS at its chosen scaling.

13. Date/time fields should be unambiguous: command dates use ISO `yyyy-MM-dd`, specified times use 24-hour `HH:mm`, and formatted dates include a readable month and year. An unspecified workout time remains distinct from midnight.
14. A future shareable client summary should exclude _private contact details_ and the client's home address. Such a summary/export is not implemented in v1.6.
15. The product is for a single user; it should not support concurrent access to the same data file by multiple users.
16. The product should not require the user to log in or create an account.
- **Supported desktop OS**: Windows, macOS, or Linux on an architecture supported by the bundled JavaFX runtime
- **Private contact detail**: A contact detail that is not meant to be shared with others
- **Client**: A person the trainer trains, stored as a record in Fittix
- **Session**: One completed training appointment, logged with the exercises, weights, sets and repetitions performed
- **Package**: A block of prepaid sessions (typically 10 or 20) bought by a client
- **Workout plan**: The client's current prescribed set of exercises; a client has at most one at a time
- **Diet goals**: The client's current nutrition target and optional coaching notes; a client has at most one current target record at a time

### Adding an exercise to a client's workout plan: `addex`
Adds an exercise to the workout plan of the person identified by the index number used in the last person listing.
`INDEX` and `n/NAME` are required. All other fields are optional:
| Field | Accepted value | Default when omitted |
| `w/WEIGHT_KG` | A finite, non-negative number in kg; decimals are allowed | `0` |
| `d/DAY` | A weekday name or accepted prefix; see [Weekday values](#weekday-values) | Grouped under **Day not specified** |
* `INDEX` refers to the index number shown in the displayed person list. It **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, …​
* Each prefix, including `n/`, may appear at most once.

* Only `n/`, `s/`, `r/`, `w/`, and `d/` are accepted parameter prefixes. A word made of letters followed by `/` after whitespace is treated as a parameter prefix; unknown prefixes such as `x/` or `ex/` cause `Invalid command format!`. For example, `addex 1 n/Stretch x/unexpected` is rejected without changing the plan. Plain words in `n/NAME` remain part of the exercise name.
* To use a default, omit the whole field. An empty field such as `s/` or `d/` is invalid.

* The same exercise name can appear on different days in a client's plan, for example Monday and Friday. Names are compared without regard to letter case: adding the same name twice on one day shows `This exercise already exists on this day in the workout plan.` and leaves the plan unchanged, even if sets, reps, or weight differ. Exercises under **Day not specified** share one group, so the same name can appear there only once.

* Each client can have at most **7 exercises per weekday**. Adding an eighth exercise to the same day shows `A client cannot have more than 7 exercises on the same day.` and leaves the plan unchanged. Other weekdays and clients have separate limits. Exercises under **Day not specified** are not capped.

Parameters: INDEX (must be a positive integer) n/EXERCISE_NAME [s/SETS] [r/REPS] [w/WEIGHT_KG] [d/DAY]

* If the plan already has no exercises, Fittix shows `Workout plan is already empty for Person: ` followed by that person, and makes no change.
* Otherwise Fittix clears the plan and shows `Cleared workout plan for Person: ` followed by the updated person (whose workout plan is `Empty`).
* `clearplan 1` clears the workout plan of the 1st person.
Records a completed workout session for a client, including the exercises, weights, sets, and repetitions performed. Logging a session does not change the client's workout plan.
* `INDEX` is the positive whole-number index shown in the current client list. After a `find` command, use the index shown in the search results.
* `DATE` is required and must be a valid date in `yyyy-MM-dd` format, such as `2020-01-15`. Today and past dates are accepted; future dates are rejected.
* `TIME` is optional and uses the 24-hour `HH:mm` format, from `00:00` to `23:59`. Seconds are not accepted. Omitting `t/` leaves the time unspecified.
* Provide between 1 and 30 exercise entries. Each entry requires all four values, separated by `|`, in the order `EXERCISE|WEIGHT|SETS|REPS`.
* `d/` and `t/` may each appear only once. Repeat `ex/` to record multiple exercises. Prefixed parameters may appear in any order.
* Exercise entries are stored and displayed in the order entered. Leading and trailing spaces around each exercise value are removed.
Exercise values must satisfy these rules:

| `EXERCISE` | 1 to 50 characters after Unicode NFC normalization, including at least one letter. Only letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and parentheses are allowed. Canonically equivalent accented spellings are stored in the same normalized form. |
| `WEIGHT` | A number from 0 to 1000, inclusive, in kilograms, with at most 2 decimal places. Enter the number without a unit, for example `40.25`. |
| `SETS` | A whole number from 1 to 100, inclusive. |
| `REPS` | A whole number from 1 to 1000, inclusive. |
* `log 1 d/2020-01-15 t/18:00 ex/Back squat|60|3|10 ex/Bench press|40.25|3|8`

On success, Fittix reports `Logged workout for NAME on DATE at TIME: N exercises.` The date uses an English month abbreviation, for example `16 Sep 2026`. When no time is supplied, the `at TIME` part is omitted. One entry is reported as `1 exercise`; repeated exercise entries each count toward the total. For example:
Logged workout for Priya Nair on 16 Sep 2026 at 18:00: 3 exercises.
Logged workout for Priya Nair on 16 Sep 2026: 1 exercise.
Sessions are saved with the client's details and remain available after restarting the app.
A client cannot have two sessions with the same date and time, even if their exercise entries differ.
* Two sessions on the same date with different specified times are allowed.
* Two sessions on the same date with both times unspecified are duplicates.
* An unspecified time is different from a specified time. For example, a session without `t/` and another with `t/18:00` on the same date are allowed.
* Different clients may have sessions with the same date and time.

A duplicate with a specified time is rejected with `A workout session already exists for NAME on DATE at TIME.` When both times are unspecified, Fittix reports `An unspecified-time workout session already exists for NAME on DATE. Add t/TIME to distinguish another session.` For example:
A workout session already exists for Priya Nair on 16 Sep 2026 at 18:00.
An unspecified-time workout session already exists for Priya Nair on 16 Sep 2026. Add t/TIME to distinguish another session.
If any exercise entry or other required value is invalid, the entire command is rejected. No part of that session is added.

Select a client in the list to see **Completed workouts** under **HISTORY** in the context panel. Each row shows the session's date, time, and all exercise entries. When time was omitted, it appears as `Time not specified`. Text wraps, and the details pane can be scrolled.

Sessions appear newest first by date and time, with every exercise entry shown. On the same date, a session without a time appears before sessions with a time; specified times are shown newest first, including midnight (`00:00`) last. The number beside each session is its current `SESSION_INDEX`. A client without sessions shows `No workout sessions recorded for NAME.` in the History section. The message disappears once a workout is recorded and updates when another client is selected.

The command lists every recorded session for the client at the displayed index, including exercise details. It uses the same session numbers and order as the selected-client panel. After `find`, use the client index shown in the filtered list. If no sessions have been logged, Fittix reports `No workout sessions recorded for NAME.`

Use `history CLIENT_INDEX` or the panel to find the session number. Provide the complete corrected session, including all exercises you want to keep. Omitting `t/` removes its specified time. Dates, times, exercises, and the 1-to-30 entry limit follow the `log` rules above. A new date/time combination that duplicates another session for the same client is rejected. An unchanged session is rejected without changing stored data. Once corrected, the session may move to a different displayed position; run `history` again before another edit. The client's other details and membership balance remain unchanged.
Deleting individual workout sessions is not currently supported.

Membership plans define a price and starting number of training sessions. Each client can have one assigned plan, and their remaining sessions are tracked independently of other clients on the same plan. Use the positive client index shown in the current list, including search results.

Plan names must be unique, ignoring case and extra whitespace. A name can contain 1 to 50 characters after trimming: ASCII letters, digits, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, and full stops, with at least one letter or digit. Leading and trailing spaces are removed, and repeated internal spaces are collapsed. Letters are ASCII-only, so accented or other non-ASCII letters (for example `É`) are not accepted. The stored name keeps the case you entered, but the plan list and client card render its first character in upper case, so a plan entered as `gold` is shown as `Gold`. The price must be greater than zero, with at most two decimal places, without a currency symbol or thousands separators. Starting sessions must be a whole number from 1 to 1000.
Both commands show each plan's price and starting sessions. If there are no plans, Fittix shows `No membership plans available.`
#### Assigning and removing a client's plan: `amem`, `rmem`

For a name with spaces, put the client index after the complete name. If supplied, `e/` follows the index. The expiry date must be a valid future calendar date when the plan is assigned. An assignment without `e/` has no specified expiry. The client card shows the plan name, remaining sessions, and expiry date if supplied. A past expiry date remains visible and does not automatically remove the plan or change its balance.

Assigning a plan gives the client its starting sessions. A client who already has a plan must have it removed before another can be assigned; trying to assign another leaves the existing balance unchanged. Different clients can use the same plan with separate balances and expiry dates.
Removing a plan discards that client's remaining sessions and expiry date. The client card then shows no membership plan or session balance.

The client must have an assigned plan. Each adjustment must be a whole number from 1 to 1000. The resulting balance must stay between 0 and 1000; reducing it to zero is allowed. An adjustment outside that range is rejected without changing the balance.

A plan assigned to any client cannot be deleted. Remove all its client assignments with `rmem` first. Plan names supplied to `amem` and `delmem` are matched without regard to case or extra whitespace. Command words and the `mem` or `membership` argument of `view` are case-sensitive; parameter prefixes are case-insensitive.

Deletes all membership plans and nothing else. Every plan in the catalog is removed. No other data is deleted: client records, workout plans, schedules, diet goals, and workout logs are left unchanged. The command takes no parameters.

A plan that is assigned to any client cannot be cleared. If at least one plan is still in use, `clearmem` deletes nothing and shows `Membership plans are in use and cannot be cleared. Remove all client assignments with rmem first.` Remove every assignment with [`rmem`](#assigning-and-removing-a-clients-plan-amem-rmem) first, or delete individual unreferenced plans with [`delmem`](#deleting-a-plan-delmem).
Failed membership commands leave every plan, assignment, and balance unchanged. The most common errors are:
* `A membership plan named Gold already exists.` — `addmem` with a duplicate name.
* `No membership plan named Silver exists.` — `amem` or `delmem` for an unknown plan.
* `Priya Nair already has an assigned membership plan.` — `amem` for a client who already has one.
* `Membership plan Gold is in use and cannot be deleted. Remove its assignments with rmem first.` — `delmem` for a referenced plan.
* `Membership plans are in use and cannot be cleared. Remove all client assignments with rmem first.` — `clearmem` while any plan is assigned.
* `This client has no membership plan to remove or adjust.` — `rmem`, `imem`, or `dmem` for a client without one.
* `Cannot decrease sessions below zero. The balance remains unchanged.` and `Cannot increase sessions above 1000. The balance remains unchanged.` — adjustments past the 0 to 1000 limits.
* `The membership change could not be saved. No plan, assignment, or balance was changed.` — the change could not be written to disk.

**Availability:** Available in v1.4; these commands do not work in v1.3. They let you record starting measurements, maintain dated weight records, view history, and compare the latest weight with the starting weight. The values are trainer-entered records, not a health assessment.

Use the client's positive index from the **current** list, including search results. For example, after `find Priya`, index `1` means the first displayed match. Body commands preserve that filter and numbering. Command words and prefixes are lowercase and case-sensitive; each prefix can appear only once. Prefixed fields may follow the index in any order.

The baseline records a date, weight in kilograms, and height in centimetres. All three are required, including when correcting a baseline. A client has one baseline. A different `bodybase` replaces it, retains every progress entry, and changes the reference used by comparison. The replacement date must be **earlier than every progress entry**; otherwise nothing changes. Re-entering the same date and numerical measurements is rejected as already current.

Fittix reports `Created body baseline for NAME: DATE; Weight: WEIGHT kg; Height: HEIGHT cm.` or `Replaced body baseline for NAME: DATE; Weight: WEIGHT kg; Height: HEIGHT cm.` Height is baseline information; later records measure weight only.

Record the baseline first. Each progress date must be later than its baseline and no later than today. You can enter weekly, daily, irregular or older measurements; there is no enforced seven-day interval.

There is one progress entry per date per client. Reusing a date **replaces the entire entry**, including notes. For example, `bodylog 1 d/2020-01-08 w/74.60` corrects that weight and removes its old notes. Omit `n/` for no notes; a blank `n/` is invalid. Re-entering identical date, weight and notes is rejected. Notes are case-sensitive, so a capitalization correction is allowed.

Fittix reports `Recorded body progress for NAME on DATE: WEIGHT kg.` or `Replaced body progress for NAME on DATE: WEIGHT kg.` A backdated entry does not become the latest measurement merely because you entered it last.

Selects that client and reveals their body-progress history in the **Body progress** card in the right context column. Scroll the workspace to read the complete history or comparison. It shows the baseline separately, then **all** progress entries in date order, oldest first, with weight and notes. The baseline is not counted as an entry. Missing notes appear as `—`. Long notes wrap; scroll vertically to read older or longer records.

Successful feedback is `Showing body progress history for NAME: N entries.` With only a baseline, it displays the baseline and `No body progress entries recorded.` With no baseline, it selects the requested client and shows `No body baseline recorded for NAME. Use bodybase first.` These empty views do not change data.

`bodyhistory` and `bodycompare` only read the loaded records: they do not write the client data file or add, remove or clear undo/redo steps. Viewing remains available when the client data file cannot be written, provided the app has loaded it successfully.
#### Comparing the latest weight with the baseline: `bodycompare`

Selects that client and reveals the comparison section. "Latest" means the greatest measurement date, regardless of recording/edit order. Fittix shows both dates and weights, the baseline height for context, and `latest weight - baseline weight`. For the example baseline and two progress entries above, the comparison reads:
A gain uses `+`, a loss uses `-`, and no change is `0.00 kg`. Fittix does not decide whether a change is healthy or desirable. It does not compare height or calculate BMI or percentage change.

Feedback is `Showing body progress comparison for NAME.` Without progress entries, it selects the requested client and shows `No body progress entries recorded for NAME. Use bodylog before comparing.` Without a baseline, it uses the missing-baseline message above. Replacing/deleting entries or correcting the baseline refreshes the comparison.

Deletes only the progress entry on that date for that client. **There is no confirmation step.** Shared [undo](#undo-redo) can restore the deleted entry while this change remains in the current session's 50-step history. Recovery through that history is unavailable after restart or once the step is discarded. The baseline and all other entries remain. To correct a wrong date, record the correct entry with `bodylog` and delete the old date. To correct weight/notes on the same date, use `bodylog` directly.

Fittix reports `Deleted body progress for NAME on DATE.` Deleting the latest entry makes the next greatest date the latest. Deleting the last entry keeps the baseline and restores the no-progress view. `bodydelete` cannot delete a baseline; use `bodybase` to correct it.
* Dates must be real dates in `yyyy-MM-dd`, years 0001–9999, and today or earlier in the computer's local time zone. `bodylog` additionally requires a date strictly after the baseline.
* Weight must be greater than 0 and at most **500 kg**. Height must be greater than 0 and at most **300 cm**. Both allow up to two decimal places. These are input limits, not medical thresholds.

* Enter measurements without units, signs, commas or exponent notation: `75`, `75.5`, `75.50` are accepted; `+75`, `.5`, `75.`, `75.500`, `75kg`, `1e2`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected. Measurements display with two decimal places.

* Supplied notes must contain 1–300 printable Unicode code points after outer horizontal whitespace is removed. A supplementary character such as `😀` counts as one; a combined symbol can contain several code points. Internal spacing and case are preserved. Line breaks and nonprintable characters are rejected.
* A separated prefix token such as `w/`, `n/` or `ex/` is reserved, including inside notes. Repeated/unsupported prefixes are rejected. Slashes inside words, such as `km/day`, are ordinary text.

Invalid mutations and failed saves leave all previous data unchanged. Successful changes select the affected client and refresh their details after saving. Baseline, weights and notes survive restarting the app; data files created before this feature load with no body tracker. A wrong local clock can cause date validation/loading failures, so check it before entering or opening dated records.

Body commands preserve contacts, other plans, schedules, logged workouts and membership balances. Deleting a client or using `clear` removes body records with the client. Shared [undo](#undo-redo) can restore these records while the change remains in the current session's 50-step history; restarting or discarding the step removes that recovery route. `clearmem` affects membership plans only. Charts, additional measurements and a dedicated tracker undo/redo command are outside this feature's v1.4 scope.

Records one payment received from a client and shows that client's payment history on their information card. Payments are independent of membership plans: recording a payment does not change a plan, its price, or the client's remaining sessions.
* `PERSON_INDEX` is a positive whole-number index in the **current** client list, including search results. An index outside that list is invalid.

* `a/AMOUNT` is required. It must be greater than zero and have at most two decimal places, without a currency symbol, sign, or thousands separator. `150`, `150.5`, and `150.50` are accepted; `0`, `-5`, `1.234`, and `S$150` are rejected. Amounts are stored and displayed with exactly two decimal places without floating-point rounding.

* `d/YYYY-MM-DD` is required. It must be a real Gregorian date in exactly four-digit-year, two-digit-month, two-digit-day form, with the year between 0001 and 9999. Past, current, and future dates are accepted.

* `r/REMARKS` is optional. After trimming outer whitespace it must contain 1 to 300 printable characters. Internal spacing, punctuation, and case are preserved. A blank `r/` is invalid, as are line breaks and control characters. Non-breaking spaces (for example U+00A0) are treated as ordinary spaces, so a remark made up of only such characters is rejected as blank. Omit `r/` when no remarks are needed.

* `a/`, `d/`, and `r/` may appear in any order after the index, but each may appear only once. The command word and prefix letters are case-sensitive. Missing, repeated, unknown, empty, or uppercase prefixes and extra unprefixed text are rejected. Parameter-shaped tokens such as `x/100` or `abc/100` inside remarks are rejected as unknown prefixes; ordinary slash-separated text such as `and/or` and `1/2` remains valid.

On success, Fittix saves the record, selects the client, and reports `Recorded payment for NAME: AMOUNT on YYYY-MM-DD.` The client's **Payments** section shows every saved record oldest first, keeping entry order for records on the same date. Each record shows its date, its amount to two decimal places, and remarks when present. Long remarks wrap and the card scrolls; they are never truncated. A client with no payments shows `No payments recorded.`

Every successful `pay` creates a separate record, even when the date, amount, and remarks are identical. Records survive unrelated edits and application restarts. Deleting a client or using `clear` removes that client's payments with the client.
| Missing index, repeated/unknown/empty prefix, or extra text | `Invalid command format!` followed by the `pay` usage |
| Invalid amount | `Amount must be greater than zero and have at most two decimal places.` |
| Invalid date | `Payment date must be a valid date in YYYY-MM-DD format.` |
| Invalid supplied remarks | `Remarks must contain 1 to 300 printable characters without line breaks when r/ is supplied.` |
| Index outside the displayed list | `The person index provided is invalid.` |
| Saving fails | `Payment could not be saved. No payment was recorded.` |
A failed command adds no payment to saved or in-memory data and creates no undo step.

Reverses the most recent saved data change, or restores a change that was undone. The complete address book is restored, including clients, workout plans, diet plans, schedules, membership data, body progress, and payments.
Neither command accepts parameters; extra text is rejected.

* Every successful command that changes saved data creates exactly one undo step. Read-only commands such as `list`, `find`, and `help`, commands that fail, and commands that leave saved data unchanged create no step.

* `undo` restores the state immediately before the most recent saved change and saves the restored state. It reports `Undid the last change.` If no step is available, it reports `No changes to undo.` without changing data.
* `redo` restores the state replaced by the most recent undo and saves it. It reports `Redid the last change.` If no step is available, it reports `No changes to redo.` without changing data.
* A new successful data-changing command after an undo clears the redo history. Read-only and failed commands leave redo history available.
* After a successful `undo` or `redo`, the full unfiltered client list is shown so restored clients are visible. Window settings and the saved data file location are not reversed.
* If saving a restored state fails, the in-memory address book and the undo/redo history remain unchanged.
* History retains up to **50 saved data changes**. When a new change exceeds this limit, the oldest undo step is discarded.
* Undo/redo history exists only for the current session. Restarting Fittix loads saved data but starts with empty undo and redo histories; changes from an earlier session cannot be undone.
The `undo` removes the new payment and the `redo` restores it.

Fittix automatically saves successful data changes. You do not need to save manually. The read-only `bodyhistory` and `bodycompare` commands display loaded records without writing the client data file.

Workout exercises, their sets, reps, weight, and assigned weekdays are restored when you reopen the app. Exercises saved without a day, including older entries labelled `day not specified` or `Day not specified`, appear together under the single **Day not specified** heading.
Membership plans and each client's plan name, remaining sessions, and expiry date are restored the same way. An assignment whose expiry date has passed is still shown so you can act on it.
### If saved client data cannot be loaded

Fittix stops startup if an existing client data file cannot be read or validated. It does not open an empty roster that could overwrite the original file. The terminal error identifies the file and explains that startup stopped to protect it.

Before changing anything, back up the file. Check the computer's date and time zone: a workout recorded as today in one time zone can appear future-dated in another. Correct the settings or restore a known valid backup, then restart. A missing data file still starts with sample clients. Use a separate empty folder if you need a fresh test session; keep the original file intact for recovery.

Client data is saved automatically in `data/addressbook.json` relative to the terminal's current folder when Fittix is launched. This is the Fittix home folder described in [Quick start](#quick-start); it need not be the folder containing the JAR. Exit Fittix before editing the file so a later save cannot overwrite your manual changes. Advanced users may edit this JSON file directly after making a backup.

If your changes make the data file invalid, Fittix stops startup and leaves that file untouched. Restore a valid backup or correct the invalid data before restarting. Always back up the file before editing it.

Furthermore, certain edits can cause the AddressBook to behave in unexpected ways (e.g., if a value entered is outside of the acceptable range). Therefore, edit the data file only if you are confident that you can update it correctly.
**Q**: How do I transfer my data to another computer?

**A**: Exit Fittix on both computers. Back up the destination's existing data, then copy `data/addressbook.json` from the old Fittix home folder to the new one. Launch Fittix from the new home folder. This transfers client records and membership plans; undo/redo history is not transferred. Do not combine two data files by overwriting one unless you intend to replace its records.

1. **When using multiple screens**, if you move the application to a secondary screen, and later switch to using only the primary screen, the GUI will open off-screen. The remedy is to delete the `preferences.json` file created by the application before running the application again.
